source: Phase 41 (2026-10-18): original questions on the chapters of Beast Academy Levels 1-5 and the AoPS books, written by Claude Sonnet from our own chapter summaries (docs/question-bank-beast-academy.md) and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.BA5.03: All text, whole-number answers (two decimal/mixed items: one 6.6). Six skills: evaluating an expression, combining like terms, the distributive property, one-step equations, two-step equations, equations from stories. No exponents or equations with the unknown on both sides.
notes.BA5.04: All text; data are written out as lists. Six skills: mean, median, mode, range, missing value from a mean, and how adding/changing a value changes the statistics. Some answers are decimals such as 5.5 or 12.5.
notes.BA5.05: Seven skills, about 14 questions each, spread over the three difficulties. All text-only. Answers to GCF/LCM/number-of-factors questions were also cross-checked by script.
notes.BA5.06: Seven skills, 33 per difficulty (R4, M5, X5, D5, V5, O5, S4). All text-only. Every fraction answer was cross-checked by script with exact arithmetic.
notes.BA5.07: Arithmetic sequences are covered by the first six skills; multiplying patterns by "Patterns that multiply" (whole-number results only). Sums use the pairing idea and no formula is named.
notes.BA5.08: Ratios and rates are written with whole-number quantities; a few answers are decimals only where the question asks time (2.5 hours). Money is in words (dollars). Average speed is tested without formulas beyond total distance over total time.
notes.BA5.11: All text, no figures. Five skills: whole numbers, fractions and decimals, estimating between two whole numbers, solving x^2 = a number (positive solutions unless the question asks how many), and calculating with square roots. A few d2/d3 questions use the negative solution of x^2 = a number.
notes.BA5.12: All text, no figures. Seven skills: evaluating powers, multiplying powers of one base, dividing powers of one base, powers of powers, the zero exponent, comparing powers, and the last digit of a power. Exponents are whole numbers (no negative exponents); a few d3 questions rewrite 4, 8 or 9 as a power of 2 or 3 to reach a common base.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.solution: A cube has a top, a bottom and four sides: 6 faces.

solve.work: A cube has 6 square faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, right.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: How many vertices (corners) does a rectangular box have?
questions.solution: A box has 4 corners on its top and 4 on its bottom: 4 + 4 = 8.

solve.work: A box has 4 corners on top and 4 on the bottom: 8.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: How many edges does a cube have?
questions.solution: There are 4 edges around the top, 4 around the bottom and 4 going up the sides: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

solve.work: 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom, 4 vertical: 12.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A solid has 2 triangle faces at its ends and 3 rectangle faces joining them. What is the solid?
questions.solution: Two matching triangle ends joined by rectangles is a triangular prism. A pyramid has only one base and the rest of its faces meet at a point.

solve.work: 2 triangular ends joined by 3 rectangles is a triangular prism.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a square base and triangle faces that meet at the top. How many faces does it have in all, counting the base?
questions.solution: The square base is 1 face and there are 4 triangle faces: 1 + 4 = 5.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
questions.solution: It has a triangle at each end, and each triangle has 3 corners: 3 + 3 = 6.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: The base of a pyramid has 4 sides. How many triangle faces does the pyramid have?
questions.solution: Each side of the base has one triangle face rising from it, so there are 4 triangle faces.

solve.work: One triangle per side of the base: 4.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: Which of these solids has exactly 6 faces?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 faces. A triangular prism and a square pyramid each have 5, and a triangular pyramid has 4.

solve.work: Triangular prism 5, triangular pyramid 4, square pyramid 5, cube 6. Only the cube.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: How many edges does a triangular pyramid have?
questions.solution: The triangle base has 3 edges, and 3 more edges go up from its corners to the top point: 3 + 3 = 6.

questions.stem: A box is 2 cm long, 3 cm wide and 4 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Multiply length, width and height: $2 \times 3 \times 4 = 24$.

questions.stem: The bottom layer of a box holds 12 cubes. The box is 3 layers tall and completely full. How many cubes are in the box?
questions.solution: There are 12 cubes in each of 3 layers: $12 \times 3 = 36$.

questions.stem: A cube has edges that are each 5 cm long. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.

questions.stem: A box is 10 inches long, 2 inches wide and 5 inches tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $10 \times 2 \times 5 = 100$.

questions.stem: A box is only 1 cm tall. Its flat bottom is 7 cm by 8 cm. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $7 \times 8 \times 1 = 56$.

questions.stem: Which unit is used to measure the volume of a box?
questions.solution: Volume counts cubes that fill a space, so it is measured in cubic units such as cubic meters.

solve.work: Volume is measured in cubic units: cubic meters.

questions.stem: The bottom of a block has an area of 20 square centimeters. The block is 3 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume is base area times height: $20 \times 3 = 60$.

questions.stem: A shed is 3 meters long, 2 meters wide and 2 meters tall. How many cubic meters of air fit inside it?
questions.solution: $3 \times 2 \times 2 = 12$.

questions.stem: Each of the 6 faces of a cube has an area of 4 square centimeters. What is the surface area of the cube in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Add the areas of the 6 faces: $6 \times 4 = 24$.

questions.stem: Which measure tells how much wrapping paper is needed to cover all the faces of a box?
questions.solution: Covering the outside of a solid is its surface area. Volume is the space inside.

solve.work: Covering all faces is surface area.

questions.stem: The top and bottom of a box each have an area of 12 square inches. The front and back each have 6 square inches. The two sides each have 8 square inches. What is the surface area of the box in square inches?
questions.solution: Add all six faces: $12 + 12 + 6 + 6 + 8 + 8 = 52$.

solve.work: 2 x (12 + 6 + 8) = 52. (Consistent with a 3 x 4 x 2 box.)

questions.stem: What is the surface area of a cube with edges of 5 meters, in square meters?
questions.solution: One face is $5 \times 5 = 25$ square meters, and a cube has 6 faces: $6 \times 25 = 150$.

questions.stem: Every face of a cube is covered with stickers. Each face has 3 rows of 3 stickers. How many stickers cover the whole cube?
questions.solution: One face has $3 \times 3 = 9$ stickers, and there are 6 faces: $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.stem: A box is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. What is the area of its top face in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The top face is 4 cm by 3 cm: $4 \times 3 = 12$.

solve.work: Top face is length x width = 4 x 3 = 12.

questions.stem: Kim paints every face of a cube-shaped box except the bottom. Each face has an area of 16 square feet. How many square feet does she paint?
questions.solution: She paints 5 faces: $5 \times 16 = 80$.

questions.stem: What is the surface area of a cube with edges of 2 cm, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each face is $2 \times 2 = 4$, and there are 6 faces: $6 \times 4 = 24$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A cube is built from small cubes with 2 small cubes along each edge. How many small cubes does it have?
questions.solution: $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: How many small cubes are needed to build a cube that is 3 small cubes long, 3 wide and 3 tall?
questions.solution: $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A layer of cubes has 4 rows with 5 cubes in each row. A tower has 3 such layers. How many cubes are in the tower?
questions.solution: One layer has $4 \times 5 = 20$ cubes, so 3 layers have $20 \times 3 = 60$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A cube is made of small cubes, with 4 small cubes along each edge. How many small cubes are in its bottom layer?
questions.solution: The bottom layer is a square 4 cubes by 4 cubes: $4 \times 4 = 16$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: Which number of small cubes can be put together to make one bigger cube?
questions.solution: $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$, so 8 small cubes make a cube. The other numbers are not of the form $n \times n \times n$.

solve.work: Cube numbers: 1, 8, 27... Only 8 is a cube (2x2x2).

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: Mia has 30 building cubes. She builds the biggest solid cube she can. How many cubes does she use?
questions.solution: $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$ fits, but $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$ is too many. She uses 27.

solve.work: Cube numbers up to 30: 1, 8, 27 (64 too big). 27.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A box is built from 1-inch cubes. It is 5 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 2 cubes tall. How many cubes does it use?
questions.solution: $5 \times 2 \times 2 = 20$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: How many small cubes make up the bottom layer of a cube that is 5 small cubes long, 5 wide and 5 tall?
questions.solution: The bottom layer is $5 \times 5 = 25$ small cubes.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A prism has a hexagon (6 sides) for each of its two ends. How many faces does the prism have?
questions.solution: There are 2 hexagon ends and 6 rectangles around the sides: $2 + 6 = 8$.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: The two ends of a prism are pentagons (5 sides). How many edges does the prism have?
questions.solution: Each pentagon has 5 edges, which is 10, and 5 more edges join the two ends: $10 + 5 = 15$.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A pentagonal pyramid has a pentagon base and triangle faces that meet at one top point. How many vertices does it have?
questions.solution: The base has 5 corners, plus the top point: $5 + 1 = 6$.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: Which of these solids has the most edges?
questions.solution: A cube has 12 edges, a triangular prism 9, a square pyramid 8 and a triangular pyramid 6.

solve.work: Square pyramid 8, triangular prism 9, triangular pyramid 6, cube 12. Cube.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: The base of a pyramid is an octagon (8 sides). How many edges does the pyramid have in all?
questions.solution: The base has 8 edges, and 8 more run from its corners to the top point: $8 + 8 = 16$.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A prism has 12 vertices. What shape are its two ends?
questions.solution: The 12 vertices are shared between 2 ends, so each end has $12 \div 2 = 6$ corners. The ends are hexagons.

solve.work: A prism with n-gon ends has 2n vertices; 2n = 12 so n = 6: hexagons.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: Maya makes a model of a rectangular box with clay balls for the vertices and sticks for the edges. How many balls and sticks does she use altogether?
questions.solution: A box has 8 vertices and 12 edges: $8 + 12 = 20$.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A box is 2 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm, and its top face is 3 cm by 4 cm. How many faces of the box, including the top itself, are exactly the same size as the top face?
questions.solution: The bottom is the same size as the top. The other four faces measure 2 by 3 or 2 by 4, so they are different. The top and the bottom make 2 faces.

solve.work: Faces come in pairs: 3x4 (top and bottom), 2x3, 2x4. Two faces are 3x4.

questions.stem: A fish tank is 40 cm long, 25 cm wide and 30 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
What is the volume of a box that is 6 cm long, 5 cm wide and 9 cm tall, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $6 \times 5 \times 9 = 30 \times 9 = 270$.

questions.stem: A box has a volume of 144 cubic centimeters. Its bottom is 8 cm by 6 cm. How tall is the box in centimeters?
questions.solution: The bottom area is $8 \times 6 = 48$. Height $= 144 \div 48 = 3$.

questions.stem: A box is 7 inches long and 5 inches tall, and its volume is 210 cubic inches. How wide is it in inches?
A cube has a volume of 64 cubic centimeters. How long is each edge, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Since $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$, each edge is 4 cm.

questions.stem: A cereal box is 20 cm long, 8 cm wide and 30 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
Dale pours water into an empty square tank whose bottom is 10 cm by 10 cm. The water is 7 cm deep. How many cubic centimeters of water are in the tank?
questions.solution: The water forms a box $10 \times 10 \times 7 = 700$ cubic centimeters.

questions.stem: Box P is 4 cm by 5 cm by 6 cm. Box Q is 3 cm by 7 cm by 5 cm. Which statement is true?
choices: Box Q holds 15 cubic centimeters more than Box P.
The two boxes hold the same amount.
Box P holds 5 cubic centimeters more than Box Q.
Box P holds 15 cubic centimeters more than Box Q.
questions.answer: Box P holds 15 cubic centimeters more than Box Q.
questions.solution: Box P: $4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120$. Box Q: $3 \times 7 \times 5 = 105$. The difference is $120 - 105 = 15$ and Box P is bigger.

solve.answer: Box P holds 15 cubic centimeters more than Box Q.

questions.stem: A box is 5 cm wide, twice as long as it is wide, and 3 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The length is $2 \times 5 = 10$ cm. Volume $= 10 \times 5 \times 3 = 150$.

questions.stem: A closed box is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Faces: top and bottom $2 \times 15 = 30$; front and back $2 \times 10 = 20$; two sides $2 \times 6 = 12$. Total $30 + 20 + 12 = 62$.

questions.stem: What is the surface area of a box that is 6 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Pairs of faces: $6 \times 4 = 24$, $6 \times 3 = 18$ and $4 \times 3 = 12$. Each pair counts twice: $2 \times (24 + 18 + 12) = 108$.

questions.stem: A closed cardboard box is 10 inches long, 8 inches wide and 4 inches tall. How many square inches of cardboard cover it, ignoring flaps and overlaps?
An open box has no lid. It is 7 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm tall. How many square centimeters of material make it?
questions.solution: Bottom: $7 \times 5 = 35$. Two long sides: $2 \times 21 = 42$. Two short sides: $2 \times 15 = 30$. Total $35 + 42 + 30 = 107$.

questions.stem: The surface area of a cube is 96 square centimeters. How long is each edge, in centimeters?
questions.solution: One face is $96 \div 6 = 16$ square centimeters. Since $4 \times 4 = 16$, each edge is 4 cm.

questions.stem: Pam paints all the faces of a block of wood that is 6 cm by 6 cm by 10 cm. How many square centimeters does she paint?
questions.solution: Two square ends: $2 \times 36 = 72$. Four rectangles: $4 \times 60 = 240$. Total $72 + 240 = 312$.

questions.stem: A box has a square bottom that is 4 cm by 4 cm, and it is 9 cm tall. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The top and bottom are $2 \times 16 = 32$. The four sides are $4 \times (4 \times 9) = 144$. Total $32 + 144 = 176$.

questions.stem: The volume of a cube is 27 cubic centimeters. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Since $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$, each edge is 3 cm. Each face is 9 and $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: Cubes with edges of 2 cm are packed to make a big cube with edges of 10 cm. How many small cubes are used?
questions.solution: Along each edge: $10 \div 2 = 5$ small cubes. Total $5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A box is 12 cm long, 8 cm wide and 6 cm tall. It is completely filled with cubes of edge 2 cm. How many cubes fit?
questions.solution: The cubes make $12 \div 2 = 6$, $8 \div 2 = 4$ and $6 \div 2 = 3$ along the three edges: $6 \times 4 \times 3 = 72$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A big cube is made from 64 small cubes. How many small cubes are along each edge?
questions.solution: Since $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$, there are 4 along each edge.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: Tom builds a cube 4 small cubes long, 4 wide and 4 tall. He removes the whole top layer. How many small cubes are left?
questions.solution: The cube had $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$ cubes and the top layer has 16. $64 - 16 = 48$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: How many more small cubes are needed to turn a cube that is 3 cubes on each edge into a cube that is 4 cubes on each edge?
questions.solution: $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$ and $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$. The extra cubes are $64 - 27 = 37$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A crate is 20 cm long, 15 cm wide and 10 cm tall. How many cubes with edges of 5 cm fit inside it exactly?
questions.solution: Along the edges: $4$, $3$ and $2$ cubes. $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: Each layer of a box holds 24 cubes. The box is exactly full with 120 cubes. How many layers tall is the box?
questions.solution: $120 \div 24 = 5$ layers.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A 3 by 3 by 3 cube is made of 27 small cubes, and its whole outside is painted. How many small cubes have no paint on them at all?
questions.solution: Only the one cube in the very middle is hidden from every side, so 1 cube has no paint.

solve.work: Only the centre cube (1x1x1 interior) is unpainted: 1.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A prism has 21 edges. How many faces does it have?
questions.solution: A prism with an $n$-sided end has $3n$ edges. $3n = 21$ gives $n = 7$. It has 2 ends and 7 side rectangles: $2 + 7 = 9$ faces.

solve.work: Prism with n-gon ends has 3n edges; n = 7; faces n + 2 = 9.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A pyramid has 14 edges. How many vertices does it have?
questions.solution: A pyramid with an $n$-sided base has $2n$ edges (n around the base and n up the sides). $2n = 14$ gives $n = 7$. Vertices: $7 + 1 = 8$.

solve.work: Pyramid has 2n edges; n = 7; vertices n + 1 = 8.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A prism and a pyramid have bases with the same number of sides. The prism has 6 more edges than the pyramid. How many sides does the base have?
questions.solution: If the base has $n$ sides, the prism has $3n$ edges and the pyramid has $2n$. The difference is $n$, so $n = 6$.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A square pyramid is glued by its square base onto one face of a cube, and the base is exactly the size of that face. How many faces does the new solid have?
questions.solution: The cube has 6 faces but the glued face is hidden, leaving 5. The pyramid adds its 4 triangles: $5 + 4 = 9$.

solve.work: Cube 6 faces, one covered: 5 remain; plus 4 triangles (slanted, not coplanar with cube faces) = 9.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A toy is a cube with a square pyramid on top. The pyramid's base is exactly the cube's top face. How many edges does the toy have on its surface?
questions.solution: The cube has 12 edges (the top four are also the pyramid's base edges). The pyramid adds 4 edges from the base corners to its tip: $12 + 4 = 16$.

solve.work: Cube 12 edges (the 4 top edges stay edges, as the slanted triangles meet the cube sides at an angle) + 4 slant edges = 16.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: A pyramid has 10 vertices. A prism has ends with the same shape as the pyramid's base. How many edges does the prism have?
questions.solution: The pyramid has $10 - 1 = 9$ base corners, so the base has 9 sides. A prism with 9-sided ends has $3 \times 9 = 27$ edges.

solve.work: 10 vertices = base of 9 sides + apex. Prism with 9-gon ends has 27 edges.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: Which of these solids has the same number of faces as vertices?
questions.solution: A square pyramid has 5 faces and 5 vertices. A cube has 6 and 8, a triangular prism 5 and 6, and a pentagonal prism 7 and 10.

solve.work: Square pyramid 5 faces, 5 vertices. Others: pentagonal prism 7/10, triangular prism 5/6, cube 6/8.

questions.skill: Faces, edges and vertices of solids
questions.stem: Every edge of a pentagonal prism is 3 cm long. A wire frame is made from all of its edges. How many centimeters of wire are needed?
questions.solution: A pentagonal prism has $5 + 5 + 5 = 15$ edges, so $15 \times 3 = 45$ cm of wire.

questions.stem: Two boxes are joined face to face with no overlap. One is 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm and the other is 2 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm. What is the total volume of the joined solid in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$ and $2 \times 3 \times 5 = 30$. Together $24 + 30 = 54$.

questions.stem: The three edges of a box are three whole numbers in a row, such as 7, 8 and 9. The volume of the box is 120 cubic centimeters. How long is the longest edge, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Try $4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120$. The longest edge is 6 cm. (Smaller sets such as $3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60$ are too small.)

questions.stem: One cube has edges of 3 cm. A second cube has edges twice as long. How many times as large as the first cube's volume is the second cube's volume?
questions.solution: The first volume is $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$. The second has edges of 6 cm: $6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216$. And $216 \div 27 = 8$.

questions.stem: A pool is 10 m long, 6 m wide and 2 m deep and is full of water. A pump removes 5 cubic meters of water each minute. How many minutes does it take to empty the pool?
questions.solution: The pool holds $10 \times 6 \times 2 = 120$ cubic meters. $120 \div 5 = 24$ minutes.

questions.stem: A solid box is 8 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. A cube-shaped hole 2 cm on each edge is cut out of its middle, leaving the rest of the box. How many cubic centimeters does the remaining solid have?
questions.solution: The whole box is $8 \times 6 \times 5 = 240$. The hole is $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$. $240 - 8 = 232$.

questions.stem: A tank has a bottom of 30 cm by 20 cm. It holds water 12 cm deep. More water is poured in until it is 18 cm deep. How many cubic centimeters of water were added?
questions.solution: The water rose by $18 - 12 = 6$ cm over a $30 \times 20 = 600$ square centimeter bottom: $600 \times 6 = 3600$.

questions.stem: A box has a volume of 480 cubic centimeters. Its length is 12 cm and the area of its bottom is 96 square centimeters. What is the sum of its width and its height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Width $= 96 \div 12 = 8$. Height $= 480 \div 96 = 5$. The sum is $8 + 5 = 13$.

questions.stem: Box A has a bottom of 6 cm by 4 cm and a volume of 96 cubic centimeters. Box B has the same volume and a bottom of 8 cm by 2 cm. How many centimeters taller is Box B than Box A?
questions.solution: Box A: height $96 \div 24 = 4$. Box B: height $96 \div 16 = 6$. Box B is $6 - 4 = 2$ cm taller.

questions.stem: Every edge of a cube is made 3 times as long. How many times as large does the surface area become?
questions.solution: A cube with edge 1 has surface area 6. With edge 3 it is $6 \times 9 = 54$. And $54 \div 6 = 9$. Each face is 3 times as long and 3 times as wide.

questions.stem: A box with a square bottom 3 cm by 3 cm has a surface area of 78 square centimeters. How tall is the box in centimeters?
questions.solution: The top and bottom are $2 \times 9 = 18$. The four sides must be $78 - 18 = 60$, so each is 15. A side is 3 cm wide, so the height is $15 \div 3 = 5$.

solve.work: 2 x 9 = 18; 78 - 18 = 60 for four sides of 3h; 12h = 60; h = 5.

questions.stem: Two cubes with 2 cm edges are put side by side so they touch face to face and form one box that is 2 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm. How many fewer square centimeters is the surface area of the box than the total surface area of the two separate cubes?
questions.solution: Two separate cubes: $2 \times 24 = 48$. The box: $2 \times (4 + 8 + 8) = 40$. The difference is $8$ (the two touching faces, $4 + 4$, are hidden).

questions.stem: A cube with 4 cm edges has a small 1 cm by 1 cm by 1 cm cube cut away from one of its corners. How does the surface area of the new solid compare with the surface area of the original cube?
questions.solution: Cutting away the corner removes 3 small squares from the outside, but it uncovers 3 new small squares inside the notch. The surface area is unchanged.

solve.work: Removing a corner cube removes 3 unit squares and exposes 3 new ones: unchanged.

questions.stem: Three faces of a box that meet at one corner have areas of 12, 15 and 20 square centimeters. What is the surface area of the whole box in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The other three faces match these three, so the total is $2 \times (12 + 15 + 20) = 2 \times 47 = 94$.

questions.stem: A 2 cm cube has a 1 cm cube glued flat onto the middle of one face. What is the surface area of the new solid in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The big cube has $6 \times 4 = 24$. The small cube covers 1 square centimeter of that but shows 4 side faces and a top: $24 - 1 + 4 + 1 = 28$.

solve.work: 24 - 1 covered + 5 new faces of the small cube = 28.

questions.stem: Four boxes each have a volume of 24 cubic centimeters. Which of them has the greatest surface area?
questions.solution: 1 by 1 by 24: $2(1 + 24 + 24) = 98$. 2 by 3 by 4: 52. 2 by 2 by 6: 56. 1 by 4 by 6: 68. The long thin box has the most.

questions.stem: A closed box is 5 cm by 4 cm by h cm and its surface area is 94 square centimeters. What is h?
A room is 5 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. Sam paints the four walls and the ceiling but not the floor. How many square meters does he paint?
questions.solution: Walls: $2 \times (5 \times 3) + 2 \times (4 \times 3) = 30 + 24 = 54$. Ceiling: $5 \times 4 = 20$. Total $54 + 20 = 74$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A 4 by 4 by 4 cube made of small cubes has its whole outside painted. How many small cubes have paint on exactly one face?
questions.solution: Each face has a middle $2 \times 2 = 4$ cubes with exactly one painted face. With 6 faces, $6 \times 4 = 24$.

solve.work: Each face has (4-2)^2 = 4 such cubes; 6 x 4 = 24.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A 5 by 5 by 5 cube made of small cubes has its whole outside painted. How many small cubes have paint on exactly two faces?
questions.solution: Those cubes sit along the 12 edges, not counting the corners. Each edge has $5 - 2 = 3$ of them. $12 \times 3 = 36$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A 5 by 5 by 5 cube made of small cubes has its whole outside painted. How many small cubes have no paint on them?
questions.solution: Remove the outer layer and a $3 \times 3 \times 3$ cube of unpainted cubes remains: $27$ cubes.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A 10 by 10 by 10 cube made of small cubes has its whole outside painted. How many small cubes have paint on three faces?
questions.solution: Only the corner cubes have three painted faces, and any cube has 8 corners.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A cube with edges of 10 cm is painted all over, then cut into cubes with edges of 2 cm. How many of the small cubes have paint on exactly one face?
questions.solution: Each edge makes $10 \div 2 = 5$ small cubes. On each face the cubes with just one painted face form a $3 \times 3$ middle: 9. For 6 faces, $6 \times 9 = 54$.

solve.work: 5 small cubes per edge; per face (5-2)^2 = 9; 6 x 9 = 54.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A solid cube is made from small cubes, 6 along each edge. Dan removes every small cube that touches the outside of the big cube. How many small cubes does he remove?
questions.solution: The cube has $6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216$ cubes. What is left is a $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$ cube. He removes $216 - 64 = 152$.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: A solid cube is made from small cubes. Exactly 98 of the small cubes touch the outside of the big cube. How many small cubes are along each edge of the big cube?
questions.solution: Try 5: the cube has 125 cubes, and the inside is $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$. $125 - 27 = 98$ touch the outside. So 5 along each edge.

questions.skill: Small cubes in a larger cube or box
questions.stem: Ann stacks 1 cm cubes to make a box 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall, then paints its whole outside, including the bottom. How many small cubes have paint on exactly two faces?
questions.solution: A cube has two painted faces when it is at an end in exactly two of the three directions. Every cube is at an end in the height direction (the box is only 2 tall). So it must be at an end in exactly one of the other two. Cubes at an end of the length but in the middle of the width: $2 \times 1 = 2$. Middle of the length (2) and end of the width (2): $2 \times 2 = 4$. That is 6 positions, times 2 heights = 12.

solve.work: Height 2 so every cube is on top or bottom. Corners: 8 (three faces). Along the 4 length-4 edges: 2 each = 8; along the 4 width-3 edges: 1 each = 4; vertical edges have only corners. Two faces: 12.

questions.stem: What is $-3 + 8$?
questions.solution: Start at $-3$ and move 8 to the right: you pass 0 after 3 steps and end 5 above it, at 5.

questions.stem: At dawn the temperature was $-2$ degrees. By noon it rose 7 degrees. What was the temperature at noon, in degrees?
questions.solution: Start at $-2$ and go up 7: $-2 + 7 = 5$.

questions.stem: What is $5 - 9$?
questions.solution: Start at 5. Subtracting 5 brings you to 0, and the other 4 take you below zero, to $-4$.

questions.stem: What is $-6 - 2$?
questions.solution: Subtracting 2 moves 2 to the left of $-6$: $-8$.

questions.stem: What is $3 \times (-4)$?
questions.solution: A positive times a negative is negative: $3 \times 4 = 12$, so the answer is $-12$.

questions.stem: What is $(-5) \times (-6)$?
questions.solution: A negative times a negative is positive: $5 \times 6 = 30$.

questions.stem: What is $-20 \div 4$?
questions.solution: $20 \div 4 = 5$ and the signs differ, so the answer is $-5$.

questions.stem: What is $-18 \div (-3)$?
questions.solution: Two negative numbers give a positive quotient: $18 \div 3 = 6$.

questions.stem: Which of these products is a negative number?
questions.solution: A product is negative when exactly one factor is negative. Only $(-6) \times 7 = -42$ has one negative factor.

solve.work: Only (-6) x 7 has one negative factor: -42.

questions.stem: In a game you lose 3 points each time you miss. Dev misses 5 times. By how many points does his score change? (Use a negative number for a loss.)
questions.solution: Each miss is $-3$, and $5 \times (-3) = -15$.

questions.solution: Anything times zero is zero.

questions.solution: Multiply first: $3 \times 4 = 12$. Then $2 + 12 = 14$.

questions.stem: What is $20 - 6 \div 2$?
questions.solution: Divide first: $6 \div 2 = 3$. Then $20 - 3 = 17$.

questions.stem: Lena writes $(2 + 3) \times 4$ on the board. What number is it equal to?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $2 + 3 = 5$. Then $5 \times 4 = 20$.

questions.stem: Use the order of operations to find the value of $18 \div 3 + 3$.
questions.solution: Divide first: $18 \div 3 = 6$. Then $6 + 3 = 9$.

questions.solution: Do both multiplications first: $10 - 6 = 4$.

questions.solution: The absolute value of a number is its distance from 0, and $-9$ is 9 away from 0.

questions.stem: What is $|5|$?
questions.solution: The number 5 is 5 away from zero, so its absolute value is 5.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers has an absolute value of 6?
questions.solution: $|-6| = 6$. The absolute values of the others are 9, 3 and 12.

questions.solution: Distance from 0 is the absolute value: $|-15| = 15$.

questions.solution: $-7$ is farther left on the number line than $-1$, so $-7 < -1$. The other statements are false.

questions.solution: The integers go $\ldots, -7, -6, -5, \ldots$. The next one above $-6$ is $-5$.

questions.solution: From left to right on the number line: $-5$, then $-1$, then 0, then 3.

questions.stem: How many integers are greater than $-3$ and less than 3?
questions.solution: They are $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2$. That is 5 integers.

questions.solution: The lowest score is the one farthest to the left on the number line: $-8$, which is Cy.

questions.solution: From $-17$ move 8 to the right: $-17 + 8 = -9$.

questions.solution: Multiply first: $4 \times (-2) = -8$. Then $3 + (-8) = -5$.

questions.solution: Divide first: $12 \div 4 = 3$. Then $-8 + 3 = -5$.

questions.solution: Parentheses first: $-3 + 7 = 4$. Then $4 \times (-2) = -8$.

questions.solution: The negatives come first, with $-10$ the farthest left: $-10$, $-3$, then 0, then 4.

questions.solution: $-12$ is closer to zero than $-15$, so $-12 > -15$. The others are false.

questions.solution: The negative integers get closer to zero as they get greater, and the one nearest zero is $-1$.

questions.solution: From coldest: Burl ($-12$), Dray ($-9$), Alton ($-5$), Clyde (3). The second coldest is Dray.

questions.solution: $-5$ is greater than $-7$ and less than $-4$. $-8$ is below $-7$, and $-3$ and 5 are above $-4$.

questions.solution: The numbers from $-8$ to 8 cancel in pairs (each $-n$ with $n$) and add to 0. What is left is $9 + 10 + 11 + 12 = 42$.

questions.stem: The sum of two integers is $-3$. When the smaller is subtracted from the larger the result is 11. What is the smaller integer?
questions.solution: Let the larger be $a$ and the smaller $b$: $a + b = -3$ and $a - b = 11$. Adding gives $2a = 8$, so $a = 4$. Then $b = -3 - 4 = -7$. Check: $4 - (-7) = 11$.

questions.solution: Subtracting $-18$ means adding 18, so the number plus 18 is 5. The number is $5 - 18 = -13$.

questions.solution: Rising: $5 \times 3 = 15$. Falling: $2 \times 4 = 8$. So $-9 + 15 - 8 = -2$.

questions.solution: Three of the factors are negative, so the product is negative. The size is $3 \times 2 \times 1 \times 1 \times 2 \times 3 = 36$. So $-36$.

questions.stem: What is the product of 25 numbers that are all equal to $-1$?
questions.solution: Each pair of $-1$s multiplies to 1. Twelve pairs use 24 numbers and give 1, and the last $-1$ remains, so the product is $-1$.

questions.solution: For $x = -2$: $|-2 - 3| = |-5| = 5$. The others give 1, 2 and 11.

questions.solution: $|x| = 0$: $y = 3$ or $-3$, 2 pairs. $|x| = 1$: $x$ has 2 choices and $|y| = 2$ gives 2, so 4 pairs. $|x| = 2$: 4 pairs likewise. $|x| = 3$: $x$ has 2 choices and $y = 0$, 2 pairs. Total $2 + 4 + 4 + 2 = 12$.

questions.stem: A point on a number line is 11 units from $-7$ and is to the right of $-7$. What integer is the point?
questions.solution: Moving 11 to the right from $-7$: $-7 + 11 = 4$.

questions.stem: The numbers $-12, 7, -3, 0, -9$ and 5 are put in order from least to greatest. Which number is third?
questions.solution: In order: $-12, -9, -3, 0, 5, 7$. The third is $-3$.

questions.stem: The integers $a$ and $b$ satisfy $a < b < 0$. Which statement must be true?
questions.solution: Both are negative and $a$ is farther from zero, so $|a| > |b|$. Their product is positive, their sum is negative and $a - b$ is negative.

questions.solution: The multiples of 7 below 20 are 7 and 14. So the number is $\pm 7$ or $\pm 14$. Only $-14$ is less than $-10$.

solve.work: |x| in {7, 14} (0 excluded since x < -10); x < -10 forces -14.

questions.solution: The distance from $-9$ to 5 is 14, and half of it is 7. Starting at $-9$ and moving 7 right gives $-2$.

questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$ and $3 \times 5 = 15$, so the total is 27. (It is also $3 \times 9$.)

questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $2(x + 3)$?
questions.solution: The 2 multiplies both terms inside the parentheses: $2 \times x + 2 \times 3 = 2x + 6$.

questions.stem: $5 \times (10 + 2) = 5 \times 10 + 5 \times ?$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: The 5 multiplies both the 10 and the 2, so the ? is 2.

questions.solution: If $m$ is the first number, $m + 5 = 12$. So $m = 12 - 5 = 7$.

questions.solution: Kay's age $k$ fits $k + 3 = 11$, so $k = 8$.

questions.solution: 5 notebooks at $n$ dollars each cost $5n$ dollars, so $5n = 20$.

questions.solution: $3 + 2 \times 9 = 3 + 18 = 21$ dollars.

questions.solution: The $x$ terms: $7x + 2x = 9x$. The plain numbers: $3 - 1 = 2$. The answer is $9x + 2$.
